newsitem.title: GERMANY: Sixt stands ground in dispute with Budget.
newsitem.headline: Sixt stands ground in dispute with Budget.

text.p: Germany's leading car rental company, Sixt AG, wants to maintain a licensing contract with Budget Group Inc despite the American firm's interest in ending the agreement, Sixt said on Tuesday.
Sixt chairman Erich Sixt told Reuters that under terms of a reservation-making agreement dating back to 1982, Budget does not have the right to unilaterally end the contract.
He said that if the U.S.-based firm does want to end its relationship with Sixt that it would have to to make an "extremely, extremely favourable offer" to Sixt as compensation.
At the centre of a dispute between the two car rental firms is Budget's claim that Sixt has broken the licensing contract by making reservations for its own units elsewhere in Europe.
Under terms of the contract, Sixt was only supposed to make foreign reservations for Budget and not other car rental companies.
The Sixt chairman countered that claim, saying Sixt had made 87,000 reservations for Budget in 1996 and only a few thousand for its own units in Switzerland, France and Austria.
Sixt and Budget were to discuss their cooperation agreement on Wednesday and Sixt said he expected the pair to arrive at a deal that would preserve their relationship.
Should Budget insist on breaking the agreement, Sixt said it would seek compensation for investment it has put into the reservation-sharing scheme over the last several years.
In 1996, Sixt said it paid 6.6 million marks in licensing fees to Budget and that the figure would grow this year.
